1#main: Bearers of the bier are exempt from Keriat Shema and prayer. In it are 3 seifim. Bearers of the bier and their replacements and replacements of their replacements — whether those before the bier or those after it — once the bier needs them, they are exempt from Keriat Shema; and the rest who accompany the dead whom the bier does not need are obligated (and see in Orach Chaim siman 72).
2#main: One does not take out the dead close to Keriat Shema — whenever there is no time to take him out to burial before the time of Keriat Shema arrives; and if they began to take him out, they do not interrupt in order to read: {Rama: And one should wait from burying him until they can estimate that most of the congregation has already prayed; and there is no distinction between morning Keriat Shema and evening Keriat Shema; and some are lenient for evening since its time is the whole night (explained in Orach Chaim siman 72).}
3#main: In a place that has shoulders designated to carry the bier, they are forbidden to tie sandals lest one's sandal come undone and he be delayed from the mitzvah: {Rama: There are places where the custom is that mourners leave the house first, then relatives and the bier after them, and distant ones place the dead on the bier and take the mourners and relatives — the bier on their shoulders — and afterward the rest of the people (Kol Bo); some say when they arrive with the dead at the cemetery they stand him every four amot before burial (there and Beit Yosef); and so is practiced nowadays to stand him two or three times before they say Tzidduk HaDin; and on days they do not say Tzidduk HaDin they need not stand him (Maharil).}
